summary: Enhance your skills in credit and risk management with our comprehensive training course focused on developing a strong risk culture.
lede: Developing a risk culture in credit and risk management connects formal credit policies with the everyday behaviours and decisions of relationship managers and credit underwriters. This course builds practical capability in risk maturity assessments, Risk Appetite Statements, the Three Lines of Defense model, cognitive bias mitigation, and board-level cultural reporting. You will use Key Risk Indicators to monitor cultural health, develop a Risk Culture Dashboard, and align incentives with long-term credit stability. The course also introduces ESG factors in credit risk perception, behavioural economics for more accurate assessments, and the COBIT framework for data governance in risk reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is essential for professionals responsible for the integrity of credit operations and the long-term financial health of their institutions.
outcomes: Behavioral Bias Mitigation In Credit Decisions
modules: Credit Risk Landscape and Conduct Standards
Measuring Risk Maturity and Behavioral Drivers
The Three Lines of Defense in Credit
prerequisites: Participants should have at least three years of experience in credit analysis, risk management, or internal audit. A basic understanding of the Basel III framework and ISO 31000 principles is recommended. No programming knowledge is required, but familiarity with financial reporting and credit policy manuals is essential.
